$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right|$2$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{b} = \left(3\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}\right)2$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) \cdot \overset{→}{b} =27$

\left\${\text{as}\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) = \overset{→}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{a} \times \overset{→}{c}\right)\right\}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) - \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}\right) = \overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{b}\right) - \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}$

questions.q:
Let $a$ and $b$ be two unit vectors such that \left| \left(a + b\right) + 2 \left($a $\times$b\right)\right| = 2$.~If \theta \in \left($0, $\pi\right)~is the angle between $\overset{^}{a}$~and $\overset{^}{b}$, then among the statements:
\left($S1\right): $2\left|\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right|
\left($S2\right)$~: The projection of $\overset{^}{a}$~on \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)~is~$\dfrac{1}{2}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left|\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) + 2 \left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right| =$2, $\theta \in \left($0, $\pi\right)

Squaring both side we get,

\left(\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) +$2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right) +$2\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right) =$4$

\left|\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right|$2 + 4\left|\left(\overset{^}{a} \times \overset{^}{b}\right)\right|$2 + 0 = 4$

Let the angle be \theta~between $\overset{^}{a}$~and~$\overset{^}{b}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{^}{a}\right|$2 + \left|\overset{^}{b}\right|$2 + 2\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|$cos$\theta +$4\left(\left|\overset{^}{a}\right|\left|\overset{^}{b}\right|$sin$\theta\right) =$4$

$⇒ 2 + 2cos$\theta +$4\sin^{2}$\theta =$4$

$⇒ 2 + 2cos$\theta -$4\cos^{2}$\theta =$0$

Let $cos$\theta =$t$ then

$⇒ 2t^{2} - t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2t^{2} - 2t + t - 1 = 0$

$⇒ 2t\left($t - 1\right) + \left($t - 1\right) = 0$

\left($2t + 1\right)\left($t - 1\right) = 0$

So,~$t = - $\dfrac{1}{2} or~$t = 1$

Then,~$cos$\theta = - \dfrac{1}{2}~or $cos$\theta =$1$~which is~not possible as~$0 \in \left(0, \pi\right)$

So,~$\theta = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

Now,

${S}_{1} ⇒ 2\left|a \times b\right| = 2sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \sqrt{3}$

And~\left|\overset{^}{a} - \overset{^}{b}\right| = \sqrt{1 + 1 - 2cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}$

$= \sqrt{2 - 2 \times \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$= \sqrt{3}$

${S}_{1}$~is correct.

${S}_{2}$~projection of~$\overset{^}{a}$~on~ \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{\overset{^}{a} . \left(\overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b}\right)}{∣ \overset{^}{a} + \overset{^}{b} )} = \dfrac{1 + cos\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)}{2 + 2cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Which is true, So both are true.

$Let $\overset{→}{a} = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j} + z\overset{^}{k}$

So,\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & 1 & \lambda\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} \left(\lambday -z\right) + \$overset{^}{j}\left($z - \lambdax\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(x - y\right)$

On comparing with~$13\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$~we get,

$⇒ \lambday - z = 13, z - \lambdax = - 1, x - y = - 4$

and $x + y + \lambdaz = - 21$

questions.q: $For $p > 0,$~a vector $\overset{→}{v}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \left(p + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}$ is obtained by rotating the vector $\overset{→}{v}1 = \sqrt{3}p\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ by an angle $\theta$ about origin in counter clockwise direction. If $tan\theta =  \left(\alpha\sqrt{3} -2\right)\$lleft(4\sqrt{3} +$3\right)$,~then the value of $\alpha$is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$\overset{→}{v}1 = \sqrt{3}p\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{v}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \left($p + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}$

tan\theta = \left(\$alpha\sqrt{3} -$2\$right)\lleft(4\sqrt{3} +3\right)$

~

\left|\overset{→}{v}1\right| = \left|\overset{→}{v}2\right|$

$⇒ 3p^{2} + 1 = 4 + ( p + 1{)}^{2}$

$⇒ 2p^{2} - 2p - 4 = 0$

$⇒ p^{2} - p - 2 = 0$

$⇒ p = 2, - 1$~(rejected)

Now,

$cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{→}{v}1 \cdot \overset{→}{v}2}{\left|\overset{→}{v}1\right| \cdot \left|\overset{→}{v}2\right|} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}p + ( p + 1 )}{\sqrt{( p + 1{)}^{2} + 4}\sqrt{3p^{2} + 1}}$

$⇒ cos\theta = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{13}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{112 - 24\sqrt{3}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \dfrac{\left(6\sqrt{3} - 2\right)2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3}$

$⇒ tan\theta = \dfrac{6\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \dfrac{\alpha\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3}$

$⇒ \alpha =6

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$ be three vectors such that $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}$. If the angle between the vector $\overset{→}{c}$ and the vector $3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ is $\theta$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $\tan^{2}\theta$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + k$, $\overset{→}{b} = - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}k$

Also, $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{c} \times \overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \left(\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c}\right) \times \overset{→}{a} = 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{c} = \lambda\overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} = \overset{→}{c} + \lambda\overset{→}{a}$

$⇒ - \overset{^}{i} - 8\overset{^}{j} + 2k = \left(4\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}k\right) + \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} +k\right)$

$⇒ \lambda + 4 = - 1, \lambda + {c}_{2} = - 8, \lambda + {c}_{3} = 2$

$⇒ \lambda = - 5, {c}_{2} = - 3, {c}_{3} = 7$

$⇒ \overset{→}{c} = 4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7k$

Now, finding angle we get,

$cos\theta = $\dfrac{\left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)}{\left|\left(3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\right| ⋅ \left|\left(4\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}\right)\right|}

$⇒ cos\theta = $\dfrac{12 - 12 + 7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}

$⇒ cos\theta = $\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{26} ⋅ \sqrt{74}}

$⇒ cos\theta = $\dfrac{7}{2\sqrt{481}}

$⇒ sec\theta = $\dfrac{2\sqrt{481}}{7}

$⇒ \sec^{2}\theta = $\dfrac{4 \times 481}{49}

$⇒ 1 + \tan^{2}\theta = $\dfrac{1924}{49}

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta = $\dfrac{1875}{49}

$⇒ \tan^{2}\theta \approx38 . 26$

$⇒ \left[\tan^{2}\theta\right] = \left[38 . 26\right] = 38

$
